correctness.rationale: The inverse-window/forward-channel equivalence is immediate by reversing the insertion. Adjacent palindrome windows produce identical parents; counting start components proves the upper bound. The period-four witnesses have valid starts at exactly even indices, with pairwise different parents whenever 4 does not divide k. Equality for an odd number of starts forces all even positions and hence period four, yielding exactly q(q-1) words. For k divisible by four and n=k+2, adjacent and distance-two starts cannot yield distinct parents. Finite exhaustive checks and a separate witness evaluator corroborate the proof, without replacing it.

value.rationale: Worst-case reverse-list degree is an intrinsic decoding ambiguity for palindromic duplication. The theorem determines it for infinitely many duplication lengths, classifies every maximizing received word for odd start-count over arbitrary alphabets, and exhibits a genuine modulo-four threshold failure in an otherwise matching generic upper bound. These facts refine the geometry relevant to coding bounds and are not an arbitrary finite computation.
